html:
The Orinoco is one of the great rivers of South America, about 2,140 kilometres long, flowing through Venezuela and along its border with Colombia to the Atlantic. Its basin covers about a million square kilometres, most of it in Venezuela.

It rises in the highlands on the Brazilian border, curves north and east around the old rocks of the Guiana Shield, and ends in a wide delta of swamps and channels. Its big western tributaries, such as the Meta, Guaviare and Apure, drain the llanos, the flat grassland plains. A natural channel, the Casiquiare, links it to the Amazon basin; Alexander von Humboldt mapped it in 1800.

The river has long been a road for peoples and trade. Potters of the Saladoid tradition moved from the lower Orinoco into the Caribbean islands from about 500 BCE. Peoples along it include:

  • the Warao, canoe people of the delta;
  • the Kari'na near the coast;
  • the Pumé and Achagua of the llanos;
  • the Uwottüja (Piaroa) and Piapoco of the middle and upper river.

On his third voyage in 1498 Columbus met the vast flow of fresh water from its mouth and guessed it must come from a continent. Later Spanish and English explorers searched up the river for El Dorado.
sum: The Orinoco is one of the great rivers of South America, about 2,140 kilometres long, flowing through Venezuela and along its border with Colombia to the Atlantic. Its basin covers about a million square kilometres, most of it in Venezuela.
